title: Evolution as a Process of Causal Inference
summary: Recently, the mapping of the replicator equation onto Bayes' theorem has been recognised, leading to an analogy between evolutionary dynamics and Bayesian learning. However, this analogy holds only for pure selection in infinite populations and breaks down when mutations -- a central mechanism of evolution -- are introduced. Here I propose that evolution by natural selection, at least for populations of haploid replicators in static environments, is best understood not as a learning process but as a process of causal inference.
